A commenter questioned the value of services like RingCentral for solo founders. They argued that being one person can be a competitive advantage, and that people waste money on things meant to make them look like a 'real company,' listing this service alongside ornate business cards and office space.

Responding to RingCentral's pitch of making a one-person business look large, a commenter said the bigger problem for most people is too many 'Press 9 to speak to a human' menus, not too few. They felt automated phone menus add friction rather than value.

As an alternative for UK home-based businesses, a commenter recommended Voipfone. They said it gave them a London number routed to a VoIP phone on their router, plus free voicemail-to-email and SMS notifications, so they could work from home without installing a second line.
A Hacker News submission titled 'RingCentral Support Sucks, but Why They Gotta Be So Shady?' complains about poor customer support and allegedly shady practices at RingCentral.
